text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

The panel's gender composition alone is not evidence of bias. For a group head role, client relationships, commercial acumen, and interview performance often outweigh total years of design experience, and the successful candidate was specifically commended for client relationships. 

Raising gender bias without concrete evidence will appear unprofessional and damage your industry reputation. Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting constructive feedback on how to strengthen your candidacy for future leadership roles. If written feedback or other facts later reveal procedural irregularities or double standards, you can evaluate next steps then, but questioning the panel's gender now is speculative and counterproductive.
